Configuring private link domains enables Private Access (ZPA) to identify and route traffic to applications hosted behind a private link (e.g., Azure Private Link). When enabled, Private Access evaluates CNAME records returned during DNS resolution to determine whether the destination is associated with a configured private link domain.
If the returned CNAME record matches a configured private link domain, Private Access forwards the request through the configured application segment to securely access the private resource.

blocks.heading: How Private Link Domain Resolution Works

blocks.text: When a user accesses a resource using its standard public domain name, the following sequence describes how DNS resolution and Private Access determine whether the request is routed through a private link endpoint.

blocks.item: User Access: A user attempts to access an application using its public domain name (e.g., companyserver.database.windows.net).
DNS Resolution: During DNS resolution, Private Access evaluates the returned DNS records to determine whether the resource is associated with a private link endpoint.

Private Link Resolution: DNS resolution returns a CNAME record that points to a private link alias (e.g., company.server.privatelink.database.windows.net). This alias resolves to a private IP address within the Azure virtual network.
Application Segment Matching: Private Access evaluates up to 5 CNAME records (from left to right in ascending order) in the public DNS response.

blocks.text: For private link routing to occur:

blocks.item: The resolved CNAME must match a configured private link domain.
The corresponding private link alias (e.g., *.privatelink.database.windows.net) must be defined in an application segment, including associated ports and protocols.

blocks.text: This ensures that only traffic mapped to valid application segments is routed through Private Access.

To route private resources through Private Access, you can configure a public domain (e.g., *.database.windows.net) in an application segment. However, configuring a broad domain can cause all traffic for that domain—including resources not associated with a private link—to be routed through Private Access, which can result in unnecessary or incorrect routing.
Private link domains address this issue by allowing Private Access to evaluate returned CNAME records and route only traffic that matches configured private link domains.
To configure a private link domain:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Private Access > Private Applications > Defined Application Segment.
Click the Column Menu icon (), and select Private Link Domains.

blocks.text: The Private Link Domains window opens.

blocks.item: In the Frontend Wildcard Domains for DNS Request and CNAME Match field, enter a valid private link domain.

blocks.text: For example, enter the regular expression *.database.windows.net to match Azure SQL private link domains. When the DNS response contains a matching CNAME record, the alias resolves to a private IP address within the Azure virtual network.

blocks.item: Ensure an application segment is defined under Defined Application Segments that includes the private link alias (CNAME target), such as *.privatelink.database.windows.net, along with the required ports and protocols. When the DNS response contains a matching CNAME record, Private Access evaluates up to 5 CNAMEs and routes traffic only if both the domain and application segment conditions are met.
